climate.overview_html: Copernicus C3S confirmed that September 2026 ranked as the third-warmest September in the ERA5 record, with persistently high extra-polar ocean surface temperatures sustaining one of the longest runs of above-normal SSTs in the modern observational record. The WMO’s Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 projects the Super El Niño’s Niño 3.4 SST anomaly averaging ~3.6°C for the season, with a 75% probability of the OND event exceeding the strength of any El Niño in the instrumental record since 1950; on September 19 the central equatorial Pacific already reached a record 3.05°C anomaly. Against that backdrop, an extraordinary IMO MEPC session scheduled for October 2026 is set to vote on the Net-Zero Framework for international shipping — a decision deferred from October 2025 under intense US pressure, with the Trump administration now threatening tariffs, visa restrictions and port levies against nations supporting mandatory shipping carbon pricing.

items.headline: Copernicus C3S: September 2026 Third-Warmest September on Record; Persistently High Extra-Polar Ocean Surface Temperatures; Super El Niño Signal Sustains Anomaly Streak
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service monthly bulletin confirms September 2026 ranked as the third-warmest September in the ERA5 dataset (which extends back to 1940), continuing the exceptional string of above-normal months driven by the combined effect of the Super El Niño and long-term anthropogenic warming. Extra-polar sea surface temperatures remained near record levels for the time of year, sustaining an ocean heat reservoir that has contributed to elevated tropical cyclone intensity and above-normal fire conditions across Southeast Asia. The September result leaves 2026 on track to rank as the second-warmest calendar year in the instrumental record. Global average 2-meter temperature for September remained above the 1991–2020 ERA5 reference average and above the estimated 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline for the fourteenth consecutive month.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 Forecast ~3.6°C Seasonal Average; 75% Chance OND 2026 Exceeds All Prior El Niño Events Since 1950; 3.05°C Record Anomaly on September 19; >90% Probability Very Strong Event Through Northern Hemisphere Winter
items.summary: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 presents the most definitive assessment yet of the 2026 Super El Niño's historic strength. The Niño 3.4 SST ensemble mean anomaly is forecast to average approximately 3.6°C during SON 2026. On September 19, the central equatorial Pacific Niño 3.4 index reached 3.05°C above average — the largest temperature anomaly since systematic measurement began. There is a 75% probability that the October–December 2026 event will exceed the intensity of any El Niño in the instrumental record back to 1950, and greater than 90% probability of a very strong event through Northern Hemisphere fall–winter. Key regional implications include continued drought and haze across Indonesia and the Maritime Continent, elevated flooding risk in eastern Africa, anomalous heat across northern Africa and northern South America, and above-normal Eastern Pacific cyclone activity alongside a suppressed Atlantic hurricane season.

items.source: CBC News / Al Jazeera / Environmental Defence Fund
items.headline: IMO Net-Zero Framework October 2026 Vote: US Threatens Tariffs, Visa Restrictions and Port Fees Against Supporting Nations; Extraordinary MEPC Session Due This Month; Global Shipping Decarbonization at Critical Juncture
items.summary: An extraordinary session of the IMO's Marine Environment Protection Committee is scheduled for October 2026 to vote on the Net-Zero Framework for international shipping — a decision deferred from October 2025 after US and Saudi pressure caused the MEPC to vote 57–49 to postpone adoption. The NZF aims to fully decarbonize shipping by 2050 through a Global Fuel Standard reducing marine fuel GHG intensity and a Carbon Pricing Mechanism. Prior to the October vote, the Trump administration intensified its opposition, warning it will not tolerate shipping cost increases and would retaliate with tariffs, visa restrictions and port levies against nations supporting adoption. Influential maritime states including Singapore are reportedly being told their NZF vote will be factored into live bilateral trade negotiations. If adopted, the NZF would be the first-ever mandatory carbon pricing mechanism for international shipping, which accounts for approximately 2.89% of global GHG emissions.

items.headline: Global Sea Surface Temperature Breaks All-Time Record at 21.1°C in August 2026; Previous Peak of 21.09°C Set March 2024 Surpassed at Unusual Seasonal Timing; El Niño Amplifying Decades of Anthropogenic Ocean Warming
items.summary: Global sea surface temperature reached 21.1°C on approximately August 25, 2026, surpassing the previous all-time record of 21.09°C set in March 2024. This record is particularly anomalous because global SSTs typically peak in March–April during Northern Hemisphere spring — an August record indicates the Super El Niño has added heat on top of an already elevated baseline in a way that offsets the normal seasonal cooling. Scientists emphasise that the El Niño is adding energy on top of decades of human-driven ocean warming, making the combined signal unprecedented. The sustained ocean heat reservoir has contributed to above-normal tropical cyclone intensity across the Western and Eastern Pacific in 2026, and is the primary driver of delayed wet-season onset across Southeast Asia sustaining the 2026 haze crisis. The Niño 3.4 anomaly continued rising after this date, reaching 3.05°C on September 19 — a record.

items.headline: Twin Cities Marathon Shifts Race Date Citing Climate Change Heat Risk; Joins Growing List of Major Sporting Events Adapting Calendars to Rising Autumn Temperatures
items.summary: Organizers of the Twin Cities Marathon announced a change to the race's traditional early-October start date, explicitly citing climate change-driven increases in autumn heat as a factor in the decision. The move reflects a broader trend of sporting events in North America reassessing scheduling as warming extends summer-like heat deeper into fall. For a race requiring mass participation over 26.2 miles, even moderate temperature increases at the tail of the distribution significantly raise heat-illness risk, particularly for recreational runners who make up the majority of the field. The announcement joins decisions by golf, tennis, cycling and other circuits to adjust scheduling, course lengths or safety protocols in response to rising baseline temperatures — a sign that climate adaptation is now a standard element of major event planning.

major_events.name: Typhoon Surigae (JTWC 26W / JMA No. 26) — APPROACHING KANTO AND TOKYO; ASIAN GAMES CLOSING CEREMONY AT RISK
major_events.status: TROPICAL STORM PRE-EXTRATROPICAL — Tokyo Governor issued warning October 1 of potential train and air service disruptions through October 2; storm tracking northeast toward Chubu (Aichi/Nagoya) on October 1–2 then into Kanto including Tokyo; extratropical transition forecast October 3, one day before the Asian Games closing ceremony October 4; peaked at Category 5-equivalent intensity (~240 km/h) earlier in the week before weakening substantially after encountering cooler SSTs east of Okinawa; compound flooding risk from pre-wetted soils across Honshu following Typhoon Dujuan ($22B, 162 deaths)
major_events.impact: Outdoor events in final days of Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya under active review; ~4,000 athletes and officials aboard the Costa Serena cruise ship in Nagoya Harbour at continued risk; Tokyo metropolitan area may experience heavy rain and transport disruption October 1–3; elevated landslide and river flooding risk across mountainous Honshu on rain-saturated soils

major_events.name: Hurricane Polo Remnants (Eastern Pacific) — TROPICAL MOISTURE FLOODING U.S. SOUTHWEST AND SPREADING INTO CENTRAL PLAINS
major_events.status: POST-TROPICAL — Polo made landfall in Baja California Sur at 110 mph (Cat 2-equivalent) September 30 before weakening rapidly inland; post-tropical remnants now spreading moisture northeast into central Rockies and Southern Plains on October 1; 3–5 inches forecast at some Southwest locations through the week; heavy rain extending into Texas and Oklahoma; mandatory evacuations still in effect for Rincon, Salem and Garfield, New Mexico over Rio Grande dam failure risk
major_events.impact: Flash flood watches across broad swath of Southern Plains; desert arroyos and rivers remain in flood; dam failure risk in south-central New Mexico; tropical moisture feed expected to persist into the first week of October; below-normal wildfire risk in Southwest where rain fell but above-normal risk in Northern California unaffected by Polo moisture

major_events.name: 2026 Bangkok / Thailand Floods — DRAINING; RECOVERY UNDER WAY
major_events.status: RECOVERING — All 50 Bangkok districts declared flood disaster zones September 26 following 300–330 mm of rain in 48 hours; peak flooding September 24–28; Bangkok Metropolitan Administration reported drainage progressing and expected to be largely complete within 24–48 hours as of October 1; 8 deaths; 52,000+ households inundated; 4,900 evacuated
major_events.impact: Recovery operations ongoing; traffic disruption at multiple city locations; Thai Cabinet emergency holidays ended; worst Bangkok flooding since 2011; damage assessment ongoing in hardest-hit districts of Lat Phrao, Bang Khen and Don Mueang; climate attribution notes Super El Niño significantly intensified the 2026 Southeast Asian monsoon season

major_events.name: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze — ACTIVE; SUPER EL NIÑO DELAYING WET SEASON
major_events.status: ACTIVE — ASEAN Level 3 air quality alert ongoing since August 1; >617,400 fire hotspots recorded in Indonesia as of mid-September; hotspot counts nearly double the same period in 2019; Singapore PSI in moderate-to-unhealthy range; WMO seasonal outlook forecasts continued dryness through October–November as Super El Niño delays Indonesia’s wet-season onset by 4–6 weeks relative to climatology
major_events.impact: Health advisories across Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Philippines and Vietnam; >12 million people affected; >1.4 million students on remote learning; smoke forecast to persist through October–November; agricultural burning season amplified by drought; carbon emissions from Indonesian peat fires among highest in the post-2015 record

major_events.name: Southern Africa Flooding — ACTIVE; EL NIÑO-DRIVEN OFF-SEASON MOISTURE ANOMALY
major_events.status: ACTIVE — FEWS.NET Global Weather Hazards for October 2026 reports active flooding across parts of Southern Africa in what is typically the dry season; linked to an El Niño-driven circulation anomaly directing anomalous moisture into the region against the expected seasonal signal
major_events.impact: Agricultural and infrastructure damage in affected areas; disrupting pre-harvest season in a region already under food insecurity stress; emergency response activated in affected countries; unusual dry-season flooding in Southern Africa echoes El Niño-driven anomalies recorded during 1997–98 and 2015–16

major_events.name: 2026 Europe Wildfire Season — WINDING DOWN; NEAR-RECORD BURNED AREA
major_events.status: WINDING DOWN — 678,978 ha burned as of late September (91% above 20-year EFFIS average); France alone burned ~100,000 ha, a 20-year satellite-era record; very extreme fire danger easing with autumn onset; Greece, Balkans and Caucasus maintaining elevated suppression posture through early October
major_events.impact: EU uninsured wildfire losses estimated €40–60 billion; EU Climate Insurance Alliance established September 16 as direct policy response; air quality impacts across Iberian Peninsula and southern France extended through September; season raises 2026 EU total to second-worst in satellite records after 2017

weather.overview_html: Tokyo’s Governor issued a warning October 1 advising residents that Typhoon Surigae may disrupt train and air services through October 2 as the weakened but still significant storm tracks northeast past the Chubu and Kanto regions, threatening the final days of the Asian Games and raising flooding risk across rain-saturated Honshu. Post-tropical moisture from Hurricane Polo continued to flood desert communities in the U.S. Southwest on October 1, with 3–5 inch accumulations forecast and heavy rain spreading into Texas and Oklahoma, while dam evacuation orders remain in effect in three New Mexico communities. The slow-moving nor’easter that left ~100,000 customers without power across the Northeast US and caused significant coastal flooding from Virginia to New England is finally pulling away as of October 1, though minor coastal flooding remains possible at high tide in Freeport and Stamford. FEWS.NET’s October 2026 global weather hazards update highlights El Niño-driven flooding in Southern Africa, continued heat stress in northern and eastern Africa and Hispaniola, and heavy rain in Central America.

items.source: Tokyo Metropolitan Government / WeatherNews / JMA / Korea JoongAng Daily
items.headline: Typhoon Surigae UPDATED October 1: Tokyo Governor Issues Disruption Warning; Storm Tracking Toward Kanto/Tokyo October 1–3; Extratropical Transition October 3; Asian Games Closing Ceremony October 4 at Risk; Landslide Hazard on Rain-Saturated Honshu
items.summary: Typhoon Surigae (JTWC 26W, JMA Typhoon No. 26) continued tracking northeast toward the Japanese archipelago on October 1, with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government issuing warnings of possible train and air service disruptions through October 2. The storm, which peaked at approximately 240 km/h earlier in the week before weakening sharply after encountering cooler SSTs east of Okinawa, is now a weakened tropical storm approaching the Chubu region including Aichi Prefecture — host of the closing days of the 2026 Asian Games. Extratropical transition is forecast around October 3, one day before the Games closing ceremony on October 4. The approach carries particularly elevated risk of landslides and river flooding across Honshu, whose soils remain saturated following Typhoon Dujuan — the costliest typhoon in Japanese history at $22.19 billion in damage and 162 deaths — just one week earlier.

items.headline: Nor’easter September 26–30: ~100,000 Power Outages; Significant Coastal Flooding New Jersey to New England; Waves to 15 ft Near Outer Banks; Slow-Moving Storm Lashes Northeast for 4+ Days; Pulling Away October 1
items.summary: A slow-moving, powerful nor'easter stalled along the Mid-Atlantic and New England coasts from approximately September 25–30, bringing sustained heavy rain, strong winds and significant coastal flooding to the Northeast US. Around 100,000 customers lost power at the storm's peak across New Jersey, New York and New England, with some areas receiving multiple days of continuous rain totaling upwards of 6 inches. Coastal flooding was significant from Virginia to New England, with waves reaching 12–15 feet near Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina. Residents in coastal New Jersey and New York communities were photographed kayaking down flooded streets. The storm is beginning to pull away as of October 1, but minor coastal flooding remains possible during morning high-tide cycles in Freeport, Lindenhurst, Stamford and Barnegat Light. At least one fatality was reported across the storm's multi-day duration.

items.headline: FEWS.NET Global Weather Hazards October 2026: El Niño Drives Southern Africa Flooding, Heat Stress in N. Africa and Hispaniola, Heavy Rain in Central America; Super El Niño Still Strengthening
items.summary: FEWS.NET's Global Weather Hazards assessment for October 2026 documents the far-reaching surface weather impacts of the strengthening Super El Niño. Southern Africa — typically in its dry season in October — is experiencing active flooding linked to anomalous moisture intrusion driven by altered atmospheric circulation patterns. Northern and eastern Africa, Hispaniola and northern South America face continued abnormal heat stress, affecting food production and livelihoods in areas already under food insecurity. Previously dry parts of Central America received beneficial heavy rain. The bulletin notes the Super El Niño continues to strengthen, with a greater than 90% probability of a very strong event through Northern Hemisphere fall and winter. The unusual Southern Africa dry-season flooding is among the clearest manifestations of the nonlinear regional precipitation anomalies associated with extreme ENSO events.

items.source: NPR / National Weather Service / Property Guardian
items.headline: Hurricane Polo Remnants October 1 Update: Post-Tropical Moisture Spreading from US Southwest Into Southern Plains; Dam Evacuation Ongoing in New Mexico; 3–5 Inches Forecast Some Locations; Fire Risk Below Normal in Southwest, Above Normal Northern California
items.summary: Post-tropical remnants of Hurricane Polo, which made landfall at Category 2 strength in Baja California Sur on September 30, continued spreading heavy rain and flooding across the U.S. Southwest on October 1 before advancing northeast into the central Rockies and Southern Plains. Flash flood watches remain in effect across a broad swath of the region, with 3–5 inch totals forecast at some locations. Mandatory evacuations remain in effect for the New Mexico communities of Rincon, Salem and Garfield due to dam failure risk on the Rio Grande. Heavy rain is expected to spread into Texas and Oklahoma during October 1–3. As a direct consequence of the Polo moisture, wildfire risk is below normal in the Southwest and Four Corners region, while Northern California — outside the Polo precipitation footprint — remains at above-normal risk through mid-October under Super El Niño-driven precipitation deficits.

renewables.overview_html: The week’s landmark renewables story is the Ember Global Electricity Review 2026 (released September 29–30), confirming that solar PV surpassed nuclear power globally in total generation for the first time ever in 2025 — solar reached 2,778 TWh (8.7% of global generation) against nuclear’s 2,703 TWh (8.9%) — while global solar capacity rose 27% to 2,383 GW and wind added a record 159 GW to reach 1,291 GW. Ember simultaneously found that clean energy met all of 2025’s new global electricity demand growth, with renewables overtaking coal globally — pushing fossil-fuel power generation into absolute decline for the first time in the modern record. On October 1, two significant transactions were announced: NTPC Renewable Energy Limited issued a 1,000 MW solar EPC tender in Kambadur, Andhra Pradesh, bids due November 16; and NZ Clean Energy signed a long-term PPA with Mercury for its 118 MW Masterton Solar and Energy Storage Project in New Zealand, expected to generate ~190 GWh per year.

items.source: Ember / World Nuclear Industry Status Report
items.headline: Ember Global Electricity Review 2026: Solar Surpasses Nuclear in Global Generation for First Time Ever in 2025; Solar 2,778 TWh (8.7%) vs. Nuclear 2,703 TWh (8.9%); Global Solar Capacity +27% to 2,383 GW; Wind +Record 159 GW; Renewables Overtake Coal Globally
items.summary: Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026, published alongside the World Nuclear Industry Status Report in late September, confirms that solar PV generated more electricity globally than nuclear power for the first time across all of 2025 — a historic energy milestone. Solar generation reached 2,778 TWh, up 30% year-on-year, while nuclear generated 2,703 TWh, rising only 1.1%. Solar's 8.7% global share nearly matched nuclear's 8.9%, with 510 GW of new solar capacity added in 2025 alone (raising the global total to 2,383 GW, a 27% increase). Wind capacity also reached a record installation pace at 159 GW added, bringing global wind to 1,291 GW. Most significantly, Ember finds that clean energy — solar, wind, hydro, nuclear and other low-carbon sources combined — met the entirety of 2025's new global electricity demand growth, leaving fossil-fuel electricity generation falling in absolute terms for the first time in the modern record. Renewables overtook coal to become the world's largest electricity source, a milestone widely anticipated but arriving several years ahead of most central-case projections from 2020–2022.

items.headline: Carbon Brief: Clean Energy Pushes Fossil-Fuel Power Into Reverse for First Time Ever in 2025; Renewable Milestone Arrived Years Ahead of Projections; Battery Storage Key Enabler of Higher Solar Penetration
items.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis of 2025 global electricity data highlights that fossil-fuel power generation fell in absolute terms in 2025 for the first time in the modern energy record — a structural inflection point years ahead of what major institutional scenarios from 2020 implied. The decline was driven by solar and wind growth large enough to more than satisfy all demand growth, leaving no residual demand for additional fossil generation. Carbon Brief highlights the role of battery storage as a key enabler of higher solar penetration, with co-located and standalone storage increasingly absorbing daytime surplus for evening discharge. While the global aggregate signals a turning point, several major economies including China, India and parts of Southeast Asia still have coal capacity at high utilization rates, meaning the structural decline will require sustained clean-energy additions across many years to complete.

items.headline: Solar Surpasses Nuclear Power Globally for First Time in Full-Year 2025 Generation; Nuclear Share Hits 8.8% — Lowest in ~45 Years and Half its 1996 Peak; Battery Storage Extends Solar’s Dispatchable Footprint
items.summary: PV Magazine and ESS News analyses drawing on the World Nuclear Industry Status Report and Ember data confirm solar panels produced more electricity worldwide than nuclear reactors across all of 2025. Nuclear's share of global electricity slipped to 8.8%, its lowest in approximately four and a half decades and roughly half of its 1996 peak of 17.5%. ESS News highlighted battery storage as a key enabler, with co-located and grid-scale storage absorbing daytime solar surplus for evening dispatch, effectively extending solar's dispatchable footprint. The milestone reflects solar's rapid capacity additions (510 GW in 2025) alongside stagnant nuclear expansion globally, where new construction largely offsets retirements in the US, Europe and Japan.

items.source: Solar Quarter / NTPC Renewable Energy Limited
items.headline: NTPC REL Issues 1,000 MW Solar EPC Tender in Kambadur, Andhra Pradesh; Two × 500 MW Installations; 60 km Transmission Line; 3-Year O&M Included; Bids Due November 16
items.summary: NTPC Renewable Energy Limited (NTPCREL), a wholly owned subsidiary of NTPC Green Energy Limited, issued a request for bids on October 1 for the EPC of a 1,000 MW ground-mounted solar PV project at Kambadur, Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh. The project comprises two 500 MW installations. EPC scope includes all equipment and civil works, a 60 km transmission line and three years of operation and maintenance services. Detailed tender documents will be available from October 15, bids due November 16, using a Single Stage Two Envelope process with a subsequent Reverse Auction. The Kambadur tender is part of NTPCREL's aggressive 2026 capacity expansion program — NTPC is pursuing 60 GW of renewable capacity by FY2032.

items.source: Solar Quarter / NZ Clean Energy (Foresight) / Mercury
items.headline: NZ Clean Energy Signs Long-Term PPA with Mercury for 118 MW Masterton Solar and Storage Project; ~190 GWh/Year; ~27,000 Homes; Agri-Solar Co-Existence; 100+ Construction Jobs
items.summary: NZ Clean Energy (NZCE), a portfolio company of the UK-headquartered Foresight Group, signed a long-term Power Purchase Agreement on October 1 with New Zealand electricity generator and retailer Mercury for renewable electricity from its 118 MW Masterton Solar and Energy Storage Project in the Wairarapa region of New Zealand's North Island. The project is expected to generate approximately 190 GWh per year, supplying approximately 27,000 households. The Masterton project is designed for agri-solar co-existence, with sheep grazing continuing across the site throughout operations. Construction is expected to create more than 100 jobs. The PPA provides NZCE the revenue certainty needed to proceed to construction financing, following NZCE's earlier 129 MW Darfield solar-plus-storage project in Canterbury, which signed a virtual PPA with Fonterra.

science.overview_html: The IMSI Institute’s workshop “Unpacking AI Weather Emulators” ran September 28 – October 2 at the University of Chicago, convening leading AI weather modelling researchers to examine capabilities, limitations and the operational path for neural forecast systems — a timely gathering as multiple systems have now crossed the threshold to operational deployment. The period’s landmark preprint is AICON (arXiv 2608.24651, August 25), Deutscher Wetterdienst’s fully operational global ML weather model — live since 2 March 2026 — trained on the high-resolution ICON-DREAM dataset at 13 km, 3-hour resolution using a graph attention network. In the cyclone forecasting space, Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext (open-sourced August 6 under Apache 2.0) proved the most accurate hurricane model of the 2026 Atlantic–Pacific season, adding more than 24 hours of cyclone track-and-intensity lead time over operational baselines. A new evaluation framework, PhysMetrics.Weather (arXiv 2606.10642), provides the field’s first systematic assessment of physical consistency in ML weather models across conservation budgets, spectral distributions and dynamical balances.

items.headline: IMSI Workshop “Unpacking AI Weather Emulators” September 28 – October 2, 2026: Leading Researchers Convene on Capabilities, Limitations and Operational Prospects of Neural Weather Forecasting
items.summary: The Institute for Mathematical and Statistical Innovation (IMSI) at the University of Chicago hosted the five-day workshop 'Unpacking AI Weather Emulators,' September 28 through October 2, 2026, bringing together leading researchers from operational weather centres, academic institutions and AI laboratories. Discussion topics included the accuracy and robustness of neural weather emulators relative to physics-based NWP, physical conservation properties, data assimilation integration, probabilistic forecast calibration, uncertainty quantification, and the gap between benchmark performance and real-world operational utility. The workshop is timed at the moment when multiple AI weather systems have crossed into operational status globally — DWD's AICON (since March 2026), ECMWF's operational AIFS, and WindBorne's WeatherMesh-6 — creating urgency around understanding failure modes, physical realism and integration into national forecasting workflows.

items.source: Deutscher Wetterdienst / University of Reading / LMU Munich
items.headline: AICON: DWD’s Fully Operational Global ML Weather Model Since 2 March 2026; 13 km / 3-Hour Resolution; Graph Attention Network on ICON-DREAM Reanalysis; arXiv 2608.24651
items.meta: DWD, University of Reading, LMU Munich · arXiv 2608.24651
items.summary: AICON (arXiv 2608.24651, submitted August 25, 2026) formally describes Deutscher Wetterdienst's fully operational global ML weather prediction model, which has been in continuous operational use at DWD since 2 March 2026. AICON is trained on the high-resolution, non-hydrostatic ICON-DREAM reanalysis dataset at 13 km horizontal resolution with 3-hour time steps — a finer training dataset than ERA5-based models. The model employs a graph neural network encoder-processor-decoder architecture with graph attention mechanism node updates, suited to the irregular ICON triangular grid. AICON is one of the world's first fully operational national weather service ML forecasting models alongside ECMWF's AIFS. The paper documents architecture, training procedure and medium-range verification results showing competitive performance with physics-based baselines. Authored by researchers from DWD's numerical weather prediction division, the University of Reading and LMU Munich.

items.headline: DeepMind WeatherNext Open-Sourced: Nature Paper Demonstrates +24h Cyclone Forecast Lead Time; Most Accurate Hurricane Model in 2026 Season; Predicted Melissa Rapid Intensification 5 Days Out at 80%; Three Variants Under Apache 2.0
items.summary: Google DeepMind published a Nature paper on August 6, 2026, documenting WeatherNext's state-of-the-art performance on tropical cyclone track, intensity and wind structure forecasting, simultaneously open-sourcing the code and model weights under Apache 2.0 across three variants: WeatherNext Cyclones, WeatherNext 2, and WeatherNext 2-mini. WeatherNext Cyclones gains more than 24 hours of lead time over operational baselines — 3-day cyclone forecasts matching accuracy previously only achieved at 2-day lead times. In the 2026 Atlantic-Pacific hurricane season, WeatherNext operated as the most accurate hurricane model across both basins, outperforming NHC official track guidance in multiple events. The model predicted Hurricane Melissa's rapid intensification and landfall in Jamaica approximately five days out at approximately 80% confidence. WeatherNext 2 forecasts hurricanes up to eight times faster than physics-based systems. The open-sourcing decision makes state-of-the-art cyclone AI accessible to any national meteorological service.

items.headline: WeatherMesh-6: WindBorne Systems’ AI Tops All Public Benchmarks; Up to 38% Lower RMSE Than IFS Ensemble; 4.5-Day Forecast as Accurate as IFS 1-Day; ~400 Proprietary Balloons Across 15 Global Sites; 3 km Resolution Over US/Europe
items.summary: WindBorne Systems released WeatherMesh-6 on June 1, 2026, immediately posting benchmark results showing it to be the world's most accurately-evaluated weather forecasting model, outperforming both ECMWF's IFS and AIFS ensembles across every weather parameter and lead time over a July 2025 – March 2026 evaluation window. Ensemble-mean RMSE improvements reach up to 38% over IFS and 32% over AIFS. For 2-meter temperature, WeatherMesh-6's 4.5-day forecast matches IFS's 1-day forecast accuracy — effectively gaining 3.5 days of lead time. Performance gains trace to WindBorne's proprietary data assimilation advantage: ~400 scientific weather balloons in continuous operation across 15 global launch sites, providing upper-air soundings from regions and altitudes poorly sampled by the global radiosonde network. WeatherMesh-6 produces hourly forecasts at 3 km resolution over Europe and the continental US. NOAA, the US Air Force and Navy use WindBorne balloon data in government forecast operations.

items.source: Kasteleyn, Maier, Lauer, Eyring, Gentine, Lucic
items.headline: PhysMetrics.Weather: First Systematic Evaluation Framework for Physical Consistency in ML Weather Models; Assesses Conservation Budgets, Spectral Energy Distributions and Dynamical Balances; Open-Source Release; arXiv 2606.10642
items.meta: Kasteleyn, Maier, Lauer, Eyring, Gentine, Lucic · arXiv 2606.10642
items.summary: PhysMetrics.Weather (arXiv 2606.10642, June 9, 2026) introduces the first comprehensive framework to assess physical consistency in ML weather prediction models across three categories: global conservation budgets (mass and energy), spectral energy distributions (preservation of spatial variance across scales), and multi-variable dynamical balances (geostrophic balance, hydrostatic balance). The motivation is that current MLWP models are primarily evaluated using pixel-wise error metrics like RMSE, providing no guarantee that forecasts are consistent with known physical laws — models can achieve low RMSE while violating conservation and generating dynamically inconsistent fields. The authors apply PhysMetrics.Weather to several leading MLWP models and show that performance varies significantly across physical dimensions not captured by standard benchmarks. Released as an open-source repository on GitHub, PhysMetrics.Weather is intended as a community standard for evaluating physical realism alongside forecast accuracy.

items.headline: “Missing the Butterfly and Predicting the Past”: Are Accurate AI Weather Models’ Lead-Time Advantages Features or Bugs of Predictability? arXiv 2608.25835
items.summary: A preprint (arXiv 2608.25835, August 2026) examines a fundamental tension in the interpretation of accurate AI weather models: do their exceptional deterministic skill scores reflect genuine physical predictability gains, or do they reflect artifacts of training on large-scale patterns in ways that would fail at the true limits of atmospheric predictability? The authors investigate whether ML weather models' claimed advantages over NWP at extended lead times represent physical improvements or artifacts of how predictability degrades differently in data-driven versus physics-based systems. The paper frames two key problems: the 'missing the butterfly' problem — whether AI models correctly represent the chaotic sensitivity to initial conditions that governs forecast skill — and a companion 'predicting the past' problem related to temporal leakage in benchmark evaluations. The analysis has direct implications for how operational services should interpret head-to-head comparisons between AI and NWP systems.

items.headline: WP-MIP: AI, Hybrid and Physics-Based Model Intercomparison Project for Weather Prediction; Standardized Evaluation Protocol Covering Deterministic Skill, Probabilistic Calibration, Physical Consistency and Computational Efficiency; arXiv 2604.16643
items.summary: WP-MIP (arXiv 2604.16643, April 2026) establishes a rigorous inter-system evaluation framework for AI, hybrid physics-ML and traditional NWP systems. The paper responds to the proliferation of AI weather model benchmarks conducted inconsistently across different verification periods, variable sets and baseline comparisons. WP-MIP defines evaluation protocols, verification datasets and metrics covering deterministic skill, probabilistic calibration, physical consistency and computational efficiency. Models included span pure ML systems (GraphCast, PanguWeather, FengWu, AIFS, WeatherMesh), hybrid systems (NeuralGCM, SFNO) and physics-based baselines (ECMWF IFS, GFS). By providing consistent inter-system comparisons, WP-MIP aims to give operational forecasting communities a trustworthy basis for decisions about when and how to integrate AI systems into forecasting workflows.

items.headline: Blending ML and Physics-Based Approaches for Weather and Climate: A Typology; Practical Path Combining Speed of ML with Robustness of Physics; arXiv 2605.20925
items.summary: A review preprint (arXiv 2605.20925, May 2026) provides a systematic typology of hybrid approaches blending machine learning and physics-based models for weather and climate applications. The paper categorizes approaches by degree and mechanism of physics integration — ranging from physics-informed loss functions and architecture constraints, through ML-based post-processing and bias correction of NWP output, to full online coupling of ML parameterizations within GCM dynamics. The authors argue blended approaches provide a practical path to innovation, combining ML speed and adaptability with the robustness, trust and interpretability of physics-based systems. The typology provides vocabulary and conceptual clarity for a field that has developed rapidly under inconsistent naming, and is intended to bridge atmospheric science, oceanography and climate modelling communities.

items.title: Climate Tech VC Hits $26.1 Billion in H1 2026, Up 55% Year-on-Year; AI and Earth Observation Drive Surge as Physical Risk Attracts Growth-Stage Capital
items.body_html: CTVC’s H1 2026 State of Climate Tech report documents $26.1 billion invested in climate technology in the first half of 2026, a 55% year-on-year increase, concentrated in a smaller set of larger transactions. AI infrastructure for energy efficiency and data-centre cooling was the fastest-growing subcategory; Earth observation funding tripled as AI-model developers sought proprietary real-world geospatial and atmospheric data. The State of Climate Tech H1 2026 report puts climate-linked AI investment at $6.6 billion across 304 deals, a 59% jump from H1 2025, with adaptation and physical climate risk companies attracting institutional growth-stage capital as physical climate risk shifts from forecast to lived reality.

items.title: ICEYE Raises €1 Billion Series F Led by General Atlantic; SAR Satellite Company Valued at Over €10 Billion; Expanding Climate Risk Assessment and Sovereign Intelligence Capabilities
items.body_html: Finnish radar satellite company ICEYE closed a €1 billion Series F on June 9, 2026, led by General Atlantic and valuing the company at over €10 billion — described as the largest European space company fundraise on record. Additional investors include Solidium, Tesi, Varma, Ilmarinen, Lifeline Ventures, Nokia, Qatar Investment Authority and TCV. ICEYE operates a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation providing all-weather, day/night imagery at up to 25 cm resolution, used by governments, utilities and insurers to assess extreme weather events, wildfires and flooding. Latitude Media identified ICEYE as the bellwether for adaptation-sector growth-stage investment, noting that as physical climate risk turns from forecast to lived reality, the tools to observe and respond are drawing institutional capital.

items.title: WindBorne Systems Raises $37 Million Series B at $250 Million Valuation; Khosla Ventures and Galvanize Co-Lead; Scaling Balloon Network and WeatherMesh AI to Weather Data Infrastructure
items.body_html: WindBorne Systems closed a $37 million Series B co-led by Khosla Ventures and Galvanize, with Translink Capital, Lux Capital and prior investors participating, valuing the company at $250 million and bringing total funding past $62 million. WindBorne operates ~600 proprietary scientific weather balloons across 15 global launch sites, whose upper-air soundings power WeatherMesh-6 — the AI forecasting model released June 2026 that tops all public benchmarks for global forecast accuracy, outperforming both ECMWF IFS and AIFS across every variable and lead time. WindBorne sells balloon data to NOAA (used in US government operations), the US Air Force and Navy. Series B proceeds will expand the balloon network beyond 1,000 units and continue WeatherMesh development.

items.title: Enel Closes $1 Billion Acquisition of 830 MW US Solar and Wind Portfolio from Excelsior Energy Capital; North American Renewable Capacity Reaches ~13 GW
items.body_html: Italian utility Enel completed its $1 billion acquisition of an 830 MW operating solar PV and wind portfolio in the US from Minneapolis-based Excelsior Energy Capital, closing in Q3 2026 as planned, bringing Enel’s North American renewables installed capacity to approximately 13 GW. The portfolio — comprising solar and wind assets across multiple US states — is expected to generate ~2.1 TWh annually and deliver ~$145 million in incremental EBITDA. The deal was announced in February 2026 alongside Enel’s €20 billion renewables investment plan for 2026–2028, approximately €8 billion higher than its prior target, with North America positioned as a key growth market under the plan.
